extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society / early‑modern experimental natural philosophers (anatomists, physicians, chemists, naturalists)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and reporting natural‑history, anatomical, medical, or chemical observations and experiments for learned society publication (including figures, measurements, experimental details, arguments, and responses to opponents).

rubrics_metrics.name: State explicit reasons/evidence for causal claims (e.g., animal is poisonous)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The reasons for thinking the animal pernicious, if eaten by a beast, are these: first, the disease imputed to this animal seldom or never affects the cattle but in autumn, and then only this insect is to be found; secondly, it seldom or never affects any cattle but what feed in low marshy grounds, and there only this animal frequents; thirdly, cows which are greedy feeders ... are the only creatures troubled by this worm; fourthly, the worm is very rare, and scarcely to be found in seven years, and so likewise is the distemper that proceeds from it.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When inferring causation from field observations, enumerate and report correlational criteria (seasonality, geographic/habitat specificity, affected host classes, rarity concordant with disease incidence) and record characteristic symptoms; note if no satisfactory experimental proof exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide precise measurements and comparative dimensions for specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed dimensions of a skull ('from its juncture with the nasal bones ... Q-tV inches, transversely ... 12-tV inches; in thickness about half an inch') and comparison to ordinary skulls to infer stature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report linear dimensions, thicknesses, and compare with typical ranges; use measurements to support inferential claims (e.g., estimating stature from skull size) and note proportional reasoning and its limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrate specimens with labeled figures and refer to them in text
rubrics_metrics.description: References such as 'Fig. 1, pi. 4, AB, is the worm lying on his belly ... Fig. 2, represents the worm reclined ...' and 'Fig. 3, pi. 4, represents a stone ...' are used to accompany descriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plates/figures with labels keyed to textual descriptions; refer to plate and figure numbers when describing morphology, condition, and position of parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use microscopy and detailed morphological description (with relative scales)
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopic observations: 'there flowed from the place a little thin moisture, containing in it some extremely small globules, less than -^ part of one of those which make the redness in the blood' and descriptions of transparent globules, thin vessels, and net‑like threads in brain medullary substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report observations from the microscope with comparative scales (fractions of known units such as a blood globule or hair), describe textures, shapes, and arrangements; note whether features might be postmortem artifacts (e.g., differences when specimen had been dead some time).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare homologous structures across species (comparative anatomy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author examines brains of turkey, sheep, ox, sparrows and compares cortical and medullary parts, noting similarities and differences in vessels, globules, and translucent material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine multiple species, record similarities/differences, and use cross‑species comparison to evaluate generality of observations and to support functional/anatomical inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report experimental procedures, quantities and outcomes in chemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: Account of distilling 18 oz. of gall 'from which he obtains 16 oz. of clear water by distillation, of a stinking oil, and 1 oz. of a salt earth' and descriptions of distillation methods (per balneum mariae, repetition, rectification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide experimental recipe: initial masses/volumes, apparatus or distillation method, observed fractions/products, and any yields; these details should enable replication and support theoretical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define key terms and lay out propositions before arguing
rubrics_metrics.description: Kunkel and Voight lay down propositions and definitions (e.g., propositions about whether any acid gives heat or flame; definition: 'Quod acidum sit sal fluore potitum, vim habens astringendi et coagulandi').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clear definitions and enumerate opposing propositions at the outset so replies can address each point methodically; explicit definitions prevent equivocation in polemics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use counter‑experiments and appeal to common/household experience as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Voight appeals to distillation of wine, fermentation of mead and Canary wines, and 'good housewifery, common custom, and universal experience' to argue about acids and preservation by salts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support theoretical positions with both controlled experiment and widely observed practical experience; cite counterexamples (e.g., foods that ferment without acidity) to challenge general claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure polemical scientific disputes: propositions, refutations, and point‑by‑point replies
rubrics_metrics.description: The controversy is carried by laying down propositions (three listed), followed by answers that grant some points, deny others, request experiments, and give counter‑arguments in numbered fashion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaging in scientific debate, present propositions clearly and respond itemized to each assertion; include experimental challenges and requests for demonstration where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report remedies, preparations and dosages when presenting medical cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include remedies and doses: 'antimonium diaphoreticum; as also a bark in India ... half an ounce in a glass of wine is the dose' and folk cures for cattle (bear's‑foot, rue, garlic, butter and beer; raddle mixed with butter‑milk for swine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide names of remedies, preparation details, and specific dosages when reporting therapeutic claims; distinguish professional treatments from folk remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious of anecdote and folk reasoning; seek experimental verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Author expresses skepticism: 'I am very apt to suspect that this worm is no more poison than other caterpillars' and labels some cures 'only used by the English husbandmen' or 'another fancy, and as ill grounded'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag folk cures and anecdotes as provisional; indicate when an asserted causal link lacks a 'satisfactory experiment' and avoid overinterpreting correlational anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note postmortem or preparation effects and specimen condition when interpreting observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations acknowledge specimen condition: 'This fluid matter, however, was chiefly in the brain of such turkeys, as had been dead for some time' and remarks on differing amounts of fluid depending on how long an animal had been dead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record time since death and preparation conditions since they can alter microscopic and macroscopic appearance; qualify inferences that could be artifacts of decomposition or handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate and characterize composite materials by microscopy/analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'chalk stones of the gout' were separated into three parts under the microscope (dry white irregular parts composed of long transparent figures; second sort in tough clear matter mixed with blood‑globules; third sort reddish from blood‑globules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting pathological or material samples, separate constituents, describe each fraction's appearance and composition under magnification, and relate those observations to pathological interpretation.
